TC1.Feature: GPIO negative-edge interrupt and raw-status clear on pins 8–39
TC1.Test Description: The test configures GPIO pins 8..39 as inputs with negative-edge interrupt enabled, generates a falling edge per pin via a pad drive register, waits for an ISR to service each interrupt, verifies per-pin input level and group interrupt status, clears raw status at both per-pin and group levels, and acknowledges/clears the system-level interrupt. Failures are counted on timeout, incorrect input level, missing group status bit, or uncleared status.
TC1.Remarks: Compile-time selection GPIO0 or GPIO1 chooses IRQ 87 or 88 and the corresponding system-level interrupt bits. All pads are driven high initially to establish a known state. A bounded wait uses a timeout of 5000 iterations with wait_on(10) per iteration; comments note adjustment may be required to match simulation timing.
Test Steps / Procedure: If GPIO0 is defined: call GIC_EnableIRQ(87). If GPIO1 is defined: call GIC_EnableIRQ(88).

Enable system-level GPIO interrupt: If GPIO0 defined, WRITE INTR_EN1 via macro MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1 with value LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1_GPIO0_INTR; if GPIO1 defined, WRITE MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1 with LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1_GPIO1_INTR.
Drive pads to known state: WRITE literal address 0xA0243ffc with 0xffffffff.
- Compute per-pin control address: addr1 = MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 + (i * 4).
- Configure input + negative-edge + clear: WRITE addr1 with ((1u<<20) | (1u<<18) | (1u<<16)).
Phase 2 per-pin interrupt test loop (i from 0 to 31):
- Pre-clear group raw status for this bit: WRITE MIZAR_GPIO_GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1 with wr_val.
- Enable interrupt for this bit: WRITE MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1 with wr_val.
- Generate falling edge: WRITE 0xA0243ffc with 0xffffffff; wait_on(30); WRITE 0xA0243ffc with bitwise NOT of wr_val.
- Initialize timeout = 5000. While (int_pend && timeout--) do wait_on(10).
- If (timeout == 0): print timeout error for GPIO(i+8) and increment test_err.
- Read per-pin control/status: raddr = MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 + (i * 4); rdata = READ raddr.
- Verify falling edge input level: if ((rdata & 0x1) != 0) then test_err++.
- Check raw interrupt indication: if ((rdata & 0x2) != 0x0) then:
- Read group status: rdata_grp = READ MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1.
- Clear per-pin raw status while keeping input: WRITE (MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 + (i * 4)) with ((1u<<20) | (1u<<16)).
- Clear group raw status bit: WRITE MIZAR_GPIO_GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1 with local_wr.
- Verify clear: rdata_grp = READ MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1; if (rdata_grp != 0x0) then test_err++.

- Acknowledge system-level interrupt: If GPIO0 defined: WRITE MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1 with LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO0_INTR; call GIC_ClearIRQ(87). If GPIO1 defined: WRITE MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1 with LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO1_INTR; call GIC_ClearIRQ(88).
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: The wait loop for each pin must exit due to ISR service before the timeout elapses.
After servicing a pin, the sampled input level for that pin must be low.
During service, the group interrupt status must indicate the serviced pin.
After clearing per-pin and group raw status, the group interrupt status must be zero.
System-level interrupt must be acknowledged/cleared without residual status after the handler path completes.
Overall pass requires test_err == 0 at finish.

TC2.Feature: GPIO positive-edge interrupt enable and service for pins 8–39
TC2.Test Description: The test enables positive-edge interrupt on GPIO pins 8..39, configures all pads as inputs, enables the group interrupt output, then for each pin generates a rising edge using a pad drive register while arming an ISR wait flag. The ISR validates that the group interrupt status is set, masks the group output during service, clears per-pin raw status for all 32 pins, confirms the group status is cleared, clears the system-level raw status, re-enables the group output, and acknowledges the interrupt controller. Failures include timeouts, missing group status, uncleared status, or uncleared system-level status.
TC2.Remarks: The ISR observe flag is declared volatile to ensure visibility in the wait loop. The per-pin raw clear is issued for all 32 pins during service. Timeouts are bounded to 2000 iterations with wait_on(10). System-level raw status is read back after clear to confirm deassertion.
Test Steps / Procedure: If GPIO0 is defined: call GIC_EnableIRQ(87). If GPIO1 is defined: call GIC_EnableIRQ(88).

Enable system-level GPIO interrupt: If GPIO0 defined, WRITE INTR_EN1 via MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1 with LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1_GPIO0_INTR; if GPIO1 defined, WRITE MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1 with LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1_GPIO1_INTR.
Enable positive-edge interrupt per pin: for i=0..31, WRITE (MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 + i*4) with 0x00020000.
Configure pads as inputs: WRITE GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP1..4 (MIZAR_GPIO_GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP1..4) each with 0x000000FF.
Enable group interrupt output: WRITE MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1 with 0xFFFFFFFF.
- Prepare low level: WRITE 0xA0243ffc with 0x00000000; wait_on(10).
- Timeout wait: set timeout=2000; while ((int_pend==1) && (--timeout>0)) wait_on(10).
- If (timeout==0): print timeout error, test_err++, break.
- Drive low again: WRITE 0xA0243ffc with 0x00000000; wait_on(10).
- Read group status: rdata_grp = READ MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1.
- Mask group during service: WRITE MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1 with 0x00000000.
- If ((rdata_grp & 0xffffffff) != 0) then continue; else print error and increment test_err.
- Clear raw status per-pin: for j=0..31 WRITE (MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 + j*4) with 0x00010000; wait_on(2).
- Verify group clear: rdata_grp = READ MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1; if (rdata_grp == 0x0) OK else print error and increment test_err.

- If GPIO0 defined: WRITE MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1 with LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO0_INTR; READ MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1 into rdata; if ((rdata & LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO0_INTR) != 0) print error and test_err++.

- If GPIO1 defined: WRITE MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1 with LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO1_INTR; READ MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1 into rdata; if ((rdata & LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO1_INTR) != 0) print error and test_err++.
- Re-enable group interrupt: WRITE MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1 with 0xFFFFFFFF.
- Acknowledge interrupt controller: If GPIO0 defined GIC_ClearIRQ(87); if GPIO1 defined GIC_ClearIRQ(88).
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: For each pin, the wait loop exits due to ISR service before the timeout elapses.
Group interrupt status must be non-zero when the ISR begins service.
After clearing per-pin raw status for all pins, the group interrupt status must read as zero.
System-level raw status must read as cleared immediately after the write-to-clear operation.
Overall pass requires test_err == 0 at finish.

TC3.Feature: GPIO register default values and read/write access verification
TC3.Test Description: The test first verifies reset/default values for a defined set of GPIO-related registers, skipping unreadable or excluded registers. It then performs masked write/readback checks over six data patterns across the same register set, honoring per-register read/write masks and skip controls. Results are accumulated and reported: any default mismatch or write/read mismatch increments failure counts.
TC3.Remarks: Default value check masks off bit0 before comparison. Certain registers are skipped for default and/or read/write testing via skip_rst_array and skip_array. Six test patterns are used for write/read verification with expected value computed using read and write masks combined with default values.
Test Steps / Procedure: - If (data == default_value_array[i]) pass else increment def_fail_cnt and print mismatch.
- Write phase loop i from 0 to CNT-1:
- Read/compare phase loop i from 0 to CNT-1:
- Compute exp_val = ((data_wr & read_mask_array[i] & write_mask_array[i]) | (wr_n & read_mask_array[i] & default_value_array[i])).
- If (data_rd == exp_val) pass else increment wr_fail_cnt and print mismatch.
After both checks: if (def_fail_cnt > 0 || wr_fail_cnt > 0) finish(1) else finish(0).
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: Default value check: For each non-skipped, readable register, (read_reg(addr) & 0xfffffffe) equals the documented default value; else count as default failure.

Write/read check: For each non-skipped, readable and writable register and for each data pattern, the readback masked value equals the computed expected value combining write mask, read mask, and preserved default bits; else count as write/read failure.
Overall pass requires def_fail_cnt == 0 and wr_fail_cnt == 0, producing finish(0). Any non-zero failure count produces finish(1).

Final finish() returns 1 if any failure counters are non-zero, else 0.
